item.title: China Focus: Int'l seminar explores CPC's self-governance practices, global implications
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- An international seminar on understanding the recently concluded key Communist Party of China (CPC) plenum was held in Beijing on Friday, bringing together more than 200 diplomats, think tank experts and media representatives from 105 countries and international organizations. At the seminar, a report titled "Putting the People First -- Values Underpinning Full and Rigorous Self-Governance of the CPC" was jointly released by the national high-level think tanks of the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee and Xinhua News Agency. EXPOUNDING ON THE PLENUM The seminar focused on the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, with participants discussing the CPC's achievements and the significance of full and rigorous Party self-governance, governance through institutions and rules, and principle of putting the people first. In his address, Qu Qingshan, president of the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee, said the plenary session was a highly important meeting held at a crucial stage in China's efforts to basically achieve socialist modernization. The session made strategic plans for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, fully demonstrating the CPC Central Committee's strong sense of historical initiative in strengthening the Party and the country, Qu said. Fu Hua, president of Xinhua News Agency, said that guided by the Resolution of the Central Committee of the CPC on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance, adopted at the plenum, the CPC will continue to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance from a new historical starting point, further strengthening its capacity to govern and its leadership capabilities. Fu also said that Xinhua stands ready to work with all parties to deepen systematic and theoretical research and interpretation of major issues concerning Party building in the new era and help the international community better understand China and the CPC. Lyu Yansong, Xinhua's editor-in-chief, said that as China strives to build a great modern socialist country and achieve its second centenary goal, sustained efforts to strengthen Party self-governance are essential to ensuring that the CPC remains a strong leadership core in the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The resolution adopts a systematic approach, with its various measures designed to reinforce one another in terms of objectives, implementation and outcomes, ensuring that the Party's governance practices keep pace with the times, follow established principles and embrace innovation, said Huang Yibing, vice president of the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee. SHARING INSIGHTS ON GLOBAL SIGNIFICANCE International participants shared their perspectives on the CPC's governance practices and their implications for political parties around the world. Zafar Uddin Mahmood, special representative of the prime minister of Pakistan on China affairs, said China's governance model and its ability to maintain institutional continuity, implement long-term plans and respond to new challenges have attracted widespread international attention. Patricio Giusto, executive director of the Observatory of Argentina-China Relations, said the CPC had offered an effective and resolute response to corruption from within -- one of the oldest challenges associated with political power. The CPC has built its political practice on strict discipline, stable institutional norms and sound intra-Party regulations, he said, adding that keeping power within the bounds of institutions is one of the key pillars of its success in Party governance. Josef Gregory Mahoney, a professor of politics and international relations at East China Normal University, said the CPC had long recognized that unchecked corruption and pointless formalities could erode public trust and undermine its governing capacity. The CPC regards improving intra-Party regulations as a long-term and fundamental approach to advancing full and rigorous self-governance, a practice worthy of study by political parties in other countries, he said. The seminar was co-hosted by the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee and Xinhua News Agency. ■

item.title: Chinese president appoints new ambassadors
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has appointed the following ambassadors in accordance with a decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, China's top legislature, an official statement said on Friday. Zhou Jingxing was appointed ambassador to Norway, replacing Hou Yue. Zhou Qian was appointed ambassador to the Czech Republic, replacing Feng Biao. Hou Yue was appointed ambassador to Italy and San Marino, replacing Jia Guide. Yao Fei was appointed ambassador to Kiribati, replacing Zhou Limin. Chen Haiping was appointed ambassador to Fiji, replacing Zhou Jian. Zhao Xing was appointed ambassador to New Zealand and the Cook Islands, as well as ambassador to the Island of Niue, replacing Wang Xiaolong. ■

item.title: China's digital drive delivers inclusive gains to people
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
HANGZHOU, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- For one minute on the main stage of the 2026 World Internet Conference (WIC) Wuzhen Summit in east China, a young man played a gentle piano piece that few realized was performed via a neurally controlled bionic hand, the fruit of a decade of research and development. The performer, surnamed Shi, lost his right hand in an accident at age 12. This year, he was fitted with the bionic hand developed by brain-computer interface (BCI) company BrainCo. "The hand enables independent finger movement through intuitive, low-latency control for precise two-handed piano play," said Shi, whose robotic hand features a human-like covering, at the summit held Nov. 2-5. BCI TECH RESTORES MOBILITY Over the past decade, BrainCo's team has worked with people with limb disabilities, studying their neural data, and "finally developed the sensors and algorithms that made it work," said Han Bicheng, founder and CEO of BrainCo, at the summit's main forum in Wuzhen, Zhejiang Province. The company's products allow people to write, draw and play the piano, and enable people to walk, run and even go rock climbing and surfing, said Han, noting that the company has helped over 10,000 people with limb disabilities across China regain their daily lives. Traditional BCI gear was "too complex and expensive" for daily use given faint brain signals, prompting Han to explore reimagining the tech -- the idea behind BrainCo. Han's start-up mirrors China's BCI industry, where companies are drawing on the country's robust communications networks, cloud computing and smart manufacturing systems to address challenges. RoboCT, another Zhejiang-based company, offers BCI products such as exoskeletons to people with disabilities. "While other robots handle what people don't want to do, exoskeletons empower us to do what we want to do but can't," said Zhang Jiyu, RoboCT's co-founder and chief operations officer. Compared with traditional passive device-assisted methods, rehabilitation speeds up significantly when the brain actively sends signals to drive muscles and bones via BCI tech, said Hong Xuanyu, the company's head of BCI products. Beyond cutting-edge technologies, the summit, which drew about 1,800 delegates from 138 countries and regions, also showed how digital transformation is reaching ordinary households, turning hopes into everyday realities. WATER TOWN'S WISHES COME TRUE In 2014, when the WIC was launched in Wuzhen, Xinhua reporters there asked locals one question: "What do you hope the Internet will bring you?" Some sought more business, some home convenience, others a more connected world. These scenes and comments are exhibited in a photo exhibition of this year's summit, with many of those wishes coming true. "I hope I can choose, order and have fresh vegetables delivered online," wrote Guo Yueming in 2014, who still runs her homestay in the canal town. Back then, she left before 5 a.m. every day to buy fresh ingredients, spending more than an hour on the road and much of the morning washing and preparing them. Now, she places an order on her phone before 10 p.m., and fresh produce arrives at her door by 10 the next morning. "With Internet platforms, guests feel more at ease, and we have less to worry about," said Guo, who can check room availability at a glance on her phone. Visitors, by scanning QR codes on the linens, can see the full laundry journey, number of wash cycles and even pH levels, an indicator of hygiene. At Wuzhen's Xizha Scenic Zone, visitors take turns snapping photos beneath a five-meter circular bamboo tray bearing the name "Wuzhen," framing themselves and the two Chinese characters in the same shot. Few may realize the piece was created by Qian Xinming, a local bamboo-weaving artisan. More than a decade ago, he sat on a bamboo stool outside his small shop in Xizha, splitting bamboo strips and weaving patterns. Passersby glanced in, snapped a photo and moved on, with few stopping to ask about prices or the craft itself. "I want to connect with bamboo-weaving enthusiasts around the world through the Internet," Qian wrote in 2014. Traditional bamboo-weaving culture needs to be shared with the help of new tools, or the craft "would remain trapped here," Qian recalled. Qian's son now uses AI and digital tools to document, preserve and promote bamboo weaving. Their new works have reached dozens of countries and regions. "Artisans, connected by the Internet, can turn traditional patterns into works that speak to contemporary taste and carry them beyond China," said Qian. AI DEVELOPMENT SHOULD AMPLIFY HUMAN VALUE "Today, we don't just discuss the future. We can see it," said John Hoffman, chairman and director of the Global System for Mobile Communications Association Ltd., who dubbed WIC "a small policy conversation" back in 2014. China is demonstrating "how advanced connectivity can become a universal utility like electricity and water," said Hoffman. "The opportunity is to translate this technology and leadership into inclusive prosperity, ensuring that no one is left behind." "The core of AI development should be to amplify human value and empower people," said Xi Dan, senior vice president of China's tech giant Tencent, noting that the company's inclusive AI initiatives have reached seniors, children in rural areas and women. "We aim to make BCI a daily interface for everyone over the next five to 10 years," said Han, who envisions, for instance, helping children with autism speak again and anyone struggling with insomnia get a good night's sleep. "We believe that the more open the underlying network, the warmer the technology, and the deeper the digital foundation, the more dignity ordinary lives can enjoy," said Han. ■

item.title: Xi says a growing China can be partner to help Europe tackle challenges
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker, who is on an official visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- A growing and developing China is not the source of Europe's problems, but a partner that can help Europe address its challenges, said Chinese President Xi Jinping during his meeting with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker in Beijing on Friday. Xi stressed that China and Europe should focus on areas of cooperation, resolve economic and trade frictions through dialogue and consultation, and achieve win-win results and common development. Noting that this year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Austria, Xi said trust and friendship are the valuable features of China-Austria relations, transcending differences in social systems, history, culture and development stages. He called on the two sides to consolidate political mutual trust, sustain the positive momentum of high-level exchanges, enhance mutual trust and dispel misgivings through communication, and lay a solid political foundation for future cooperation. Xi said that during the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) period, China will foster emerging industries, upgrade traditional industries, and further expand opening-up, with a focus on the service sector. China Opportunity 2.0 will bring not only market dividends but also innovation dividends, he noted. China stands ready to work with Austria to expand practical cooperation in emerging fields such as new-energy vehicles, artificial intelligence, digital economy and green development, and foster new engines for economic and trade growth, Xi said. Noting that China-Austria friendship enjoys extensive public support, Xi said the two sides should expand people-to-people and cultural exchanges, facilitate personnel flows, and bring the peoples of the two countries even closer. Stocker said that Austria is committed to fostering its friendly strategic partnership with China, and adheres to the one-China policy. Stocker called on the two countries to build on the long-standing cooperation and mutual trust to comprehensively strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, science and technology, innovation and other fields, boost cultural, tourism and other people-to-people exchanges, and elevate bilateral relations to new heights. He said Austria actively supports the development of EU-China relations and hopes both sides can resolve economic and trade differences through candid dialogue and consultation. Austria is ready to work with China to uphold multilateralism, strengthen multilateral coordination, advance sustainable development, tackle challenges including climate change, and safeguard global prosperity and stability, added Stocker. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker, who is on an official visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang)

item.title: China, Gabon elevate ties to community with shared future for new era
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping held talks with Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema in Beijing on Friday. The two leaders announced the elevation of bilateral relations to a China-Gabon community with a shared future for the new era. Noting China is willing to be a reliable friend and partner for Gabon in its independent development, Xi said China supports Gabon in maintaining independence in political, economic and diplomatic affairs, and will join hands with Gabon to build a China-Gabon community with a shared future for the new era. Xi said China is ready to work with Gabon to maintain close communication at all levels, exchange experience in political party and state governance, and support Gabon in strengthening its governance capacity. Hailing the strong economic complementarity and great potential for cooperation between the two countries, Xi called on both sides to strengthen the alignment of their development strategies and cultivate new growth drivers for cooperation. He called for making good use of the new opportunities presented by zero-tariff treatment of African goods and the "green channel" facilitation measures for African agricultural and food products exported to China. Both sides should expand and upgrade bilateral trade and investment cooperation to support Gabon's industrial development, job creation, and livelihood improvement, thereby enhancing the country's capacity for independent economic development, Xi said. "The vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity and the four major global initiatives I have proposed serve, first and foremost, the common interests of the Global South and African countries," Xi said, adding that China supports Gabon in playing a greater role in international and regional affairs. Nguema said Gabon firmly adheres to the one-China principle, and hopes to draw on China's successful experience in governance of party and country. He said Gabon stands ready to further deepen practical cooperation with China, and welcomes more Chinese enterprises to invest and do business in Gabon to help Gabon achieve industrialization and sustainable development. Noting that China has established a mutually beneficial and win-win partnership with Africa, Nguema said the zero-tariff policy meets the needs of African countries, enabling African products to enter the vast Chinese market, which is of historic significance to the development of African countries. He added Gabon is willing to work with China to enhance solidarity and cooperation between Africa and China and jointly safeguard the interests of Global South countries. After the talks, the two heads of state witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents covering the implementation of the Global Security Initiative, zero-tariff treatment, industrial and supply chains, Chinese language education, and other fields. During Nguema's state visit to China, the two sides issued a joint statement on building a China-Gabon community with a shared future for the new era. Prior to the talks, Xi held a welcome ceremony for Nguema in the Great Hall of the People. Xi also held a welcome banquet for him in the evening. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a welcome ceremony for Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema in the Northern Hall of the Great Hall of the People prior to their talks in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. item.title: China passes law against cross-border corruption, ratifies agreement on establishing World AI Cooperation Organization
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
Zhao Leji, chairman of the National People's Congress (NPC) Standing Committee, presides over the closing meeting of the 25th session of the 14th NPC Standing Committee at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Ling) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese lawmakers on Friday voted to adopt a law against cross-border corruption, a law on procuratorial public-interest litigation, and ratify an agreement on establishing the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization. The votes were taken at a closing meeting of the 25th session of the Standing Committee of the 14th National People's Congress (NPC) in Beijing. Lawmakers also voted to adopt a law on Antarctic activities and environmental protection, a revised Water Law, and a decision on amending 15 laws, including the Emergency Response Law. They also adopted a decision to remove Li Lecheng from the post of minister of industry and information technology. President Xi Jinping signed five presidential orders to promulgate the laws and the decision, and a sixth one to announce the decision on the personnel change. Zhao Leji, chairman of the NPC Standing Committee, presided over the closing meeting. The meeting also voted to adopt reports on the examination of deputies' proposals and on the qualification of certain deputies and other personnel-related bills. Addressing the closing meeting, Zhao stressed the need to uphold higher standards and adopt more concrete measures to improve the efficacy of Party building within the people's congress system, while urging further improvements to the legal framework for combating corruption. He also chaired a meeting of the Council of Chairpersons of the NPC Standing Committee before the closing meeting, and presided over a lecture for lawmakers afterward. ■

item.title: Xi replies to young Australian students
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping recently replied to 110 young Australian students who had written to him, encouraging them to remain committed to promoting the China-Australia friendship. In his letter dated Oct. 28, Xi said he was pleased to learn that the students recently visited China to take part in the Sino-Australian Collegiate Rowing and Dragon Boat Friendship Challenge, where they competed alongside Chinese university students, engaged in in-depth exchanges, forged friendships that transcended borders, and created wonderful memories together. China and Australia share a longstanding tradition of friendly exchanges, Xi noted, adding that the future of bilateral relations lies with the younger generation. He voiced hope that the Australian students can continue to actively contribute to the cause of friendship between the two countries, serve as torchbearers of the friendship and cooperation between the two countries, and carry forward this friendship from generation to generation. Recently, 110 young Australian students from the University of Sydney and other universities jointly wrote to Xi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, sharing their experiences of the China trip. They expressed admiration for China's long-lasting history and rich culture, as well as its scientific and technological innovation capabilities. They also voiced their eagerness to help carry forward the bilateral friendship and foster greater mutual understanding. ■

item.title: Xi votes in local legislative election in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, casts his ballot to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District of Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping cast his ballot at a polling station in Beijing on Friday to elect deputies to a local people's congress. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, voted at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress. Xi stressed efforts to practice whole-process people's democracy, uphold Party leadership, and strengthen oversight throughout the election process to ensure that deputies who meet the people's expectations are elected. Around 3:30 p.m. Friday, Xi arrived at the polling station, gave his voter registration card to staff for verification, and got a ballot. He cast his ballot after filling it. Noting that the election of deputies to people's congresses is an important foundation for upholding, improving and practicing the people's congress system, Xi underlined the need to give full play to democracy, strictly act in accordance with the law, and ensure that the election is carried out fairly and cleanly. On Friday afternoon, other senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi cast their ballots in person, while Han Zheng entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Former Chinese leader Hu Jintao also entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Friday saw people vote at 13,054 polling stations across Beijing to elect 4,898 new deputies to the people's congresses at the district level and 11,137 deputies to the township-level people's congresses. ■ Chinese Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, casts his ballot to elect deputies to a local people's congress at the Ziguangge polling station of the Wenjin Street electoral district in Xicheng District of Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. item.title: Xi holds talks with Sultan of Oman, stressing bilateral cooperation, peace efforts in Middle East
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Nov. 2 (Xinhua) -- President Xi Jinping said on Monday that China stands ready to work with Oman to steer their strategic partnership to a higher level, and to help restore peace and realize lasting stability in the Middle East at an early date. Xi made the remarks during talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China -- the first by Oman's head of state since the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries 48 years ago. The talks constituted an important chapter in the history of China-Oman relations and will inject strong impetus into the development of bilateral ties, Xi said. He said China and Oman should enhance political mutual trust and strengthen exchanges of experience in national governance, while expressing China's support for Oman in safeguarding national independence, sovereignty, security and stability, and in independently exploring a development path suited to its national conditions. The two sides should expand practical cooperation and continuously cement the foundation of mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation, he said, adding that China is committed to promoting high-quality development and expanding high-standard opening up, which will bring greater opportunities to Oman and other countries. China is ready to deepen the synergy of development strategies with Oman and be a stable and reliable partner in the energy sector, a partner with promising potential in investment, and a partner in fostering innovation within advanced technologies, he said. China aims to make bilateral energy cooperation more multi-dimensional and comprehensive, strengthen exchanges in industry, investment, artificial intelligence (AI), science and technology, and people-to-people ties, and join hands on the paths toward development, revitalization, and modernization, Xi said. He also called for efforts to intensify cooperation in such fields as education, tourism, health, media and sports, to continuously substantiate the China-Oman strategic partnership. Xi noted that the Middle East and the Gulf region should not become an arena for major power rivalry or geopolitical conflicts, and that concerted efforts are needed to foster and maintain peace and stability in the region. "China has been actively committed to ending hostilities and promoting peace, aiming to contribute its wisdom and solutions to resolving the regional security predicament," Xi said. China will continue to advocate resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, and support regional countries in building a common home of good-neighborliness, development, security and cooperation, he added. China is ready to strengthen communication and coordination with Oman and other Arab states and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries to jointly work for the early restoration of peace and tranquility in the region and the realization of lasting stability, Xi said. Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said that Oman firmly adheres to the one-China principle and supports China in safeguarding its national sovereignty and territorial integrity. He expressed hope that this visit will serve as a new starting point to explore more cooperation opportunities with China, and build a future-oriented partnership and promote greater development of bilateral relations. Stressing that China has been Oman's largest trading partner for many years and Chinese enterprises' investment in Oman has kept growing, Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said Oman is ready to synergize development strategies with China and strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, industry, infrastructure, AI, science and technology, and other fields. He said Oman highly appreciates China's just position on the Middle East issue and stands ready to maintain close coordination with China to uphold international law, advocate for the peaceful resolution of disputes, and jointly promote security and stability in the region and beyond. After their talks, the two leaders jointly witnessed the signing of cooperation documents covering areas including industrial and supply chains, green development and digital finance. During the visit, the two sides issued a joint statement on deepening the China-Oman strategic partnership. Prior to the talks, Xi held a welcome ceremony for Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik in the Great Hall of the People. Xi also held a welcome banquet for him at noon. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 2, 2026.
